Messages.Author: Emmit Svenson
Messages.Body:
LSJ,

Your ruling from Jan '02 says, "The vampire produced by a Caitiff
performing the Embrace (or Third Tradition or what have you) is a
Caitiff." What about Thin-Blooded Seers produced by Caitiff? Are they
Caitiff, or merely clanless?

Messages.Author: sath...@o2.pl
Messages.Body:
AFAIK Caitiff means clanless both in RPG and in VTES. So created
vampire would be Caitiff or claneless vampire of the Camarilla.

Sathriel

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


Merely clanless. TBS doesn't attempt to inherit its sire's clan, so
it wouldn't inherit its sire's Caitiffness, either.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <1132516499.4...@g47g2000cwa.googlegroups.com>,

sath...@o2.pl writes:
>AFAIK Caitiff means clanless both in RPG and in VTES. So created
>vampire would be Caitiff or claneless vampire of the Camarilla.

Caitiff and clanless are not the same thing in V:TES. All Caitiff are
clanless, but not all clanless vampires are Caitiff.

See, for example, Call the Great Beast. The vampire created by that
cannot be burned by Tradition Upheld, as it is clanless but not Caitiff.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
sath...@o2.pl wrote:
> So is Caitiff considered a clan or just a different case of being
> clanless?

Caitiff is a trait. Only clanless vampires have that trait, but not all
clanless vampires have that trait.

Like "Anarch" is a trait that some independent vampires can have.

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:


What's confusing is that Caitiff is a trait that is not represented by
trait-text. It is represented by a clan symbol and a background.
Since clan symbol normally indicates clan, it can be confusing that
Caitiff is not a clan. In hindsight, it probably would have been
better to just make Caitiff a clan, or else to consider *all* clanless
vampires to be Caitiff. Neither is the case. Hope I didn't confuse
things further... ;)
